incidents.vector: Lateral movement onto a senior finance executive's machine, then living-off-the-land Windows tools and a custom Aspose-based infostealer that exfiltrated mailbox contents to Dropbox.
incidents.impact: A senior executive's full Microsoft Outlook mailbox was repeatedly exfiltrated from August 2025 through mid-February 2026, exposing months of non-public business deals, listings information, and internal communications. Operators dropped new backdoors before losing access around March 19.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft / supply-chain worm
incidents.vector: Compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account pushed orphan commits that triggered GitHub Actions OIDC publishing, planting the 'Miasma' Mini Shai-Hulud worm variant into 32 packages with valid SLSA provenance.
incidents.impact: Trojanized @redhat-cloud-services packages (averaging ~80,000 weekly downloads) executed an obfuscated preinstall dropper that harvested GitHub, npm, AWS, Azure, GCP, Vault, and Kubernetes credentials, then self-propagated by republishing other maintainer packages. npm removed the affected versions.

incidents.victim: UN World Food Programme — Gaza aid recipients
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the WFP Self-Registration Application used in Palestine to enroll households for food and cash assistance.
incidents.impact: Personal data of roughly 600,000 Palestinian households in Gaza was exposed, including names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and neighborhood-level location details. WFP suspended the registration platform and is investigating; attribution is not yet established.

incidents.victim: Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran actors abused Meta's AI customer-support chatbot, using a near-target VPN IP to request password resets, then instructing the bot to attach an attacker-controlled email to the account.
incidents.impact: Instagram accounts of the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the U.S. Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian imagery. Several high-value short usernames were also reportedly hijacked. Meta pushed an emergency patch and secured impacted accounts.

incidents.victim: GitHub (internal repositories) and broader CI/CD ecosystem
incidents.vector: A poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (v18.95.0) was pushed via VS Code's auto-update mechanism and compromised a GitHub employee's device; a parallel 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows into public repositories.
incidents.impact: Approximately 4,000 internal GitHub repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale, and the Megalodon campaign harvested CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, and tokens across many public repos. CVE-2026-48027 was added to CISA's KEV catalog; CISA urged rotation of all CI/CD credentials.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; victim name surfaced on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal before Charter confirmed an incident.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a security breach after being listed by the ShinyHunters extortion group. Scope, dataset, and customer impact have not yet been publicly detailed.

incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of hardcoded, shared ASP.NET machineKey values (CVE-2026-5426) in KnowledgeDeliver installations, enabling crafted ViewState payloads that triggered unauthenticated remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Attackers deployed the in-memory BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) web shell, tampered with site JavaScript to push a fake security plug-in, and dropped Cobalt Strike Beacon tailored to the victim organization. Mandiant responded; Digital Knowledge has rotated keys for new installs.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access the land and real-estate data system.
incidents.impact: Roughly 600,000 records were stolen, including property data, cadastral information, and real names tied to real-estate transactions in Lithuania.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; intrusions went initially undetected.
incidents.impact: Two unnamed Vietnamese government agencies whose networks hold personal data on millions of citizens are under active investigation following undetected breaches.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor created a public GitHub account ('Private-CISA') and committed AWS GovCloud keys plus other plaintext credentials, after disabling GitHub's built-in secrets-scanning push protection.
incidents.impact: Dozens of internal CISA systems were exposed via leaked credentials, including an RSA private key granting full access to all repositories in the CISA-IT GitHub organization. More than a week after notification, CISA was still working to invalidate keys. Lawmakers opened a formal inquiry.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; Play ransomware group claims to have exfiltrated data from MyPillow's corporate network.
incidents.impact: The Play ransomware group is extorting MyPillow and claims to hold sensitive financial documents. MyPillow has not yet publicly confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Misconfigured, internet-exposed Elasticsearch database left without authentication for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal details of approximately 19 million customers — including phone numbers and full names tied to WeChat accounts — were exposed before the server was secured.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and staff
incidents.vector: Suspected account takeover of WhatsApp, consistent with an ongoing Russia-attributed campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: The WhatsApp account of independent Australian MP Zali Steggall and three of her staffers were compromised in March 2026; disclosure surfaced publicly in late May. Communications exposure and onward social-engineering risk are the primary concerns.
